My building is one of those rental company specials, the target demographic being us folks who have no room to be picky about vibes with the rent we pay, which means the design is void of personality in favor of cheap durability. The envelope is taped to the outside of my suite door.

I can't believe I briefly considered letting Miley in here. I must never let anyone in here. And something breaks deep inside me, like my whole day, or lifetime, is catching up with me at once.

When I first moved to Calgary, seven years after high school and long after most of my classmates moved away from our town, it was all so easy. Sure, my job wasn't going perfectly, but it paid. I was finally free from my parents' home -- free from the years of them trying to control me and force me back into being a person. This meant I could finally do more than hide from them in my room reading epic fantasy and crying. But most crucially, I could be anonymous.

It meant I had lived through it. Plus, I survived everything before.

I drop my bags on the counter and pour myself a healthy glass of wine, then head to the couch with my phone and open my creeper Instagram account. This is one of my favorite pastimes while drinking: checking in on what people I used to know are up to. My heart almost drops out my butt when I spot the newest post. They're all together, sitting at a picnic table with a tent in the background. Camping. The hashtags may be ironic, but they're also not: #highschoolreunion, #friends5eva. They're not wallowing or hiding in their apartments drinking alone.
beats.story_cn: 我喜欢在脑海里重播人生中最精彩的争论并赢得胜利，研究童星和他们的家庭长相，或是把遥控器这类东西拆开又装上。我把包扔在吧台上给自己倒了杯健康的葡萄酒，然后拿着手机瘫进沙发，点开那个偷窥专用的INS账号。这是我最爱的饮酒消遣之一：窥探那些故人的近况。当我看到最新动态时，心脏几乎要从屁股里坠出来——他们全都在一起，坐在野餐桌前，背景里支着帐篷。露营。那些标签或许带着讽刺，但也未必不是真心：#高中同学会 #永远的朋友。他们既没有自怨自艾，也没有躲在公寓里独自饮酒。

They have jobs, and I do too. But I should have a real Instagram. I pour myself another drink and resolve to change my profile picture to my face. I take a few selfies, only they all look weird. I'm either smiling too much or not smiling enough, looking too hard at the camera or not at all.

Their lone penises sit sadly between their legs, not so much a prize as a participation trophy. I know looking at them doesn't make me any better, but it does feel that way. A banner appears on my screen, notifying me that Armin has followed me back. Maybe he and I could be work friends.

beats.story: He's also Persian, and I'm pretty sure we're similar ages. Maybe, if I think back to when he started at the office four years ago, there were a couple times that he tried to be friendly to me. Unfortunately, I was already deep in my rut. Once, he came over to my desk and asked if I'd tried poutine from the shop across from our building, but I was too nervous to start a conversation because Charlie -- the person who used to hold Caitlin's job -- was listening in, which made it all so embarrassing. And one afternoon he pointed at my headphones and asked what I was listening to, but I was caught off guard because the true answer would've been an audiobook about souls. I didn't have it in me to explain that I'm not, like, into souls in a weird way, more just unhealthily obsessed with what other people think happens when we die, but also too logical to believe any of it, yet still hopeful that I'll find some explanation that will make what happened feel okay. So I replied, "Just a random thing," and, unintentionally, had a tone in my voice. I do know that both of our moms come from Tehran.
beats.story_cn: 他也是波斯人，我敢肯定我们年纪相仿。也许，若我回想四年前他刚来办公室时，他确实有几次试图对我表示友好。不幸的是，我那时已深陷在自己的泥潭里。有一次他走到我桌旁，问我有没有尝过街对面店里的肉汁奶酪薯条，可我当时太紧张了，没法接话——因为当时顶替凯特琳职位的查理正在旁边听着，这让我尴尬极了。还有天下午，他指着我的耳机问我听什么，我猝不及防，因为真实答案会是一本关于灵魂的有声书。我没力气解释我其实不是对灵魂有怪癖，只是病态地执着于人死后会发生什么，但又过于理性以至于无法相信任何解释，却仍抱着希望想找到某种能让我接受已发生之事的说法。所以我回答：“随便听听啦”，语气里不自觉带上了刺。我确实知道我们俩的母亲都来自德黑兰。

beats.story: Unfortunately, this discovery was unveiled during a diversity initiative that Gregory organized for the office. We were both quietly enraged that Gregory lumped us and a few others into a token group for a Q&A session to "educate the office." After the ordeal, Gregory praised himself for personally hiring us both, even though I'm certain during my interview he had no idea I was anything other than white. After that, Armin and I never mentioned anything about our Iranian backgrounds again. And I'm not even sure we should speak about it, or if Armin even believes me. I grew up with so little contact with anything Persian outside of my family, I have a hard time telling which parts of my upbringing are cultural and which are just my family. I remember how seen I felt when I was twelve and we visited another Iranian family, and they also had a watering can on their toilet tank. I can't exactly go through the logistical nightmare of bringing Armin to see my bathroom to prove it. I scroll through his account: photos from concerts in crowded bars, some of his impressive sneaker collection, and a few Twitch clips of some video game.
beats.story_cn: 遗憾的是，这一发现是在格雷戈里为办公室组织的多元文化活动上暴露的。我和他都暗自愤怒——格雷戈里把我们和另外几人归进一个“样板小组”，搞了场问答环节来“教育办公室同仁”。那场煎熬过后，格雷戈里还自夸亲自招了我们俩，尽管我敢说面试时他压根没看出我不是白人。自那以后，阿明和我再没提过我们的伊朗背景。我甚至不确定我们是否该谈论这个，或者阿明是否相信我。我成长过程中几乎没接触过家庭以外的任何波斯文化，很难分清哪些教养方式是文化熏陶，哪些只是我家的习惯。记得十二岁那年我们去另一家伊朗人做客，发现他们马桶水箱上也放着浇水壶时，那种被看见的触动。我总不能搞出这么大阵仗，带阿明来我家看浴室来证明这点。我滑动浏览他的主页：拥挤酒吧里的演唱会照片，几双令人赞叹的球鞋收藏，还有几段电子游戏的Twitch直播片段。

They do trips together, nights out with matching shirts, spa days, wine and paint nights. Do they just, like, text each other whenever? I swallow to dislodge the thing caught in my throat. Another notice: Garret would like to follow me.
beats.story_cn: 我滑动着她的主页，吞咽着那些模仿网红的生活碎片：披着Etsy买的毯式斗篷在海滩捧着杯子，每月目标用亮闪闪的花体字写在摊开的日记本上，冰沙顶上缀着精心切片的鲜果，她男友牵着她的手。永远只拍手或躯干。这样最好；至少我能想象他带着点盖伊·费里的粗犷美学。继续下划时间线时，我发现了她朋友们的照片。她们一起旅行，穿统一T恤的夜晚出游，SPA水疗日，红酒绘画之夜。她们难道随时想约就约吗？我吞咽了一下，想咽掉喉头哽住的东西。又一条通知：加勒特想关注我。
